cards.text: Jonah finally went into Nineveh and proclaimed, “Forty more days and Nineveh will be overturned!” (Jonah 3:4). Seven words, friend, SEVEN, and when God saw the people turn from their evil ways, He relented from the disaster (Jonah 3:5-10). But Jonah is greatly displeased, and he becomes angry.
So Jonah prays to the LORD, and his prayer opens with what is basically I TOLD YOU SO.

cards.question: Jonah reminds the LORD what he said back in his own country. That's why, he says, he was so quick to flee toward ___.
Jonah finally explains why he ran from going to Nineveh in the first place. What does he say he knew?

answers.text: God is gracious and relents from disaster
The Ninevites would never listen to him
The journey there was too long and dangerous

cards.text: Then Jonah lists it out: “You are a gracious and compassionate God, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion—One who relents from sending disaster.” He's reading God's best qualities out loud LIKE IT'S A COMPLAINT.

cards.question: Still angry that Nineveh was spared, Jonah makes a request. True or false: he asks the LORD to destroy Nineveh after all.

cards.text: Jonah asks the LORD to take his life, for it's better for him to die than to live. The LORD answers with one short question.

cards.question: The LORD replies to Jonah's prayer with one short question. What does He ask?

answers.text: Have you any right to be angry
Do you not remember the great fish
Will you go back to your own country

cards.text: Then Jonah leaves the city, sits down east of it, and makes himself a shelter. I bet he's sulking, friend, and I sulked for a while in the back of a junk drawer, but at least I didn't have to BUILD the drawer.

cards.question: True or false: Jonah sits in the shade of his shelter to see what will happen to Nineveh.

cards.text: But the LORD isn't done with Jonah yet. The LORD God appoints something to grow up over Jonah's head to ease his discomfort.

cards.question: What does the LORD God make grow up over Jonah's head to give him shade?
True or false: Jonah is greatly pleased with the vine the LORD God gave him.

cards.text: From greatly displeased to GREATLY PLEASED, all over one plant. Then dawn comes the next day, and God appoints something else.

cards.question: At dawn the next day, God appoints a ___ that attacks Jonah's shade plant.

cards.text: The plant withers, then God appoints a scorching east wind, and the sun beats down on Jonah's head. I work next to ovens all day, and even I'd be asking somebody for a fan.

cards.question: True or false: with the sun beating down on him, Jonah finally admits the LORD was right to spare Nineveh.

cards.text: Jonah grows faint and wishes to die, saying, “It is better for me to die than to live.” Then God asks that question again, with something new on the end: “Have you any right to be angry about the plant?”

cards.question: God asks Jonah if he has any right to be angry about the plant. What does Jonah say?

answers.text: He is angry enough to die
He is sorry he got so angry
He has no right to be angry

cards.text: Then the LORD lays it out: Jonah cared about a plant he never tended and never made grow, one that sprang up in a night and perished in a night. Friend, that's like me crying over a batch I never mixed, never baked, never even SMELLED.

cards.question: Jonah got attached to a plant he never even made grow. So what does the LORD ask Jonah next?

answers.text: Should He not care about the city of Nineveh
Why did Jonah never thank Him for the plant
Will Jonah go back into the city to preach

cards.question: True or false: along with Nineveh's people, the LORD also mentions the city's many cattle.

cards.text: More than 120,000 people who cannot tell their right hand from their left, and many cattle as well. That's the last verse of Jonah, friend, and the book ends right there, on the LORD's question.
